approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule by sampling local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves molecular formula. It sanitizes and normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first full batch allowed by its short-term inverse-motif memory. A fresh neighbor is blocked when opposite signed motif changes match restrictions from one earlier selected transition. The walk then moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a worsening move, uses canonical order for exact ties and maintains a separate best archive. Selected transitions install bounded, sign-balanced restrictions with four-step tenure and latest-origin overlap refresh. Identity repair and the nitrogen-relocation menu are retained parts of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Remove active tabu rejection for one integration contribution probe. The same motif predicate and memory history will still be recorded, allowing every evaluated neighbor that the retained rule would have blocked to be identified. The evaluated batch will instead be the first full set of valid fresh graph neighbors. Earlier siblings relaxed matching, changed which transitions or motifs received credit, preserved overlapping origins or extended restriction lifetime; each kept an active tabu gate. This experiment tests the contribution of that entire admission gate after nitrogen-relocation development. The earlier relaxation losses motivate a predicted score decrease when the gate is removed.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-abcd951ab7cc completes all supplied replicas at macro mean 0.5217591163770486 and population deviation 0.006329100643035156. Its mean gain over its own Parent is only 0.0008412882577690054, concentrated mainly in one task and seed. A passive audit of the actual fifteen task logs independently reconstructs 195 same-transition bidirectional vetoes among 4545 valid-novel tests. Relative to each recorded first-valid-novel prefix, memory changes 145 of 435 batches, displaces 172 prefix members and selects 19 next states absent from those prefixes. Two of twelve fresh nitrogen-relocation draws are vetoed. These are real exclusions beyond canonical duplicate rejection, but the supplied prefixes do not establish the score contribution of retaining them. The memory family already contains active relaxations with negative results: gain-gated credit in n-a240f72e3717 admits 74 newly evaluated neighbors and changes macro mean by -0.020273360127168; complete-live-signature matching in n-7c411fdf5a88 admits 113 and changes mean by -0.039186838732539676. Preserving overlapping origins in n-52759efc37a6 changes one scored batch and also lowers the endpoint. This evidence motivates a direct removal test of the retained gate, with the directional expectation that eliminating all structural exclusion will weaken useful trajectory redirection. The bottleneck being resolved is the unisolated contribution of a gate that still materially controls batch membership, not an assumption that its blocked molecules are poor or valuable. Passive audit .slots/SPIRAL2.r0013-02-improve-L16.plan-audit.json records the Parent source-log receipts and 24963 passing saved-record checks, without new scores or candidate execution.
hypothesis: Ablate enforcement of the retained same-transition bidirectional inverse-motif tabu gate: every graph-valid canonically fresh neighbor reaches the inherited first-full-batch admission path, while the unchanged Parent predicate and selected-transition memory lifecycle run only as passive diagnostics.

finding_summary.headline: Tabu removal admits 170 otherwise vetoed neighbors and lowers the mean score by 0.002275
finding_summary.insights: The active gate provides a small net endpoint benefit in this panel despite excluding some immediate improvements and even one molecule that becomes a Child task maximum. The result therefore rules out judging the gate solely by the quality of its excluded neighbors or by counts of local gains. Its effect develops through changed batch membership, random-stream consumption and later sources: every paired session first diverged at a common recorded neighbor vetoed by Parent and admitted by Child, but the next state sometimes stayed identical for several more batches. The effect is strongly seed- and task-dependent; the average loss is dominated by the second seed, especially sitagliptin_mpo, while two seeds improve. This is evidence for the entire gate in the tested panel, not universal necessity or an individual motif contribution. Removing restrictions also did not guarantee greater access to the retained nitrogen exchange: eligible source batches fell from 97 to 49 and accepted exchanges from ten to four; none of the four beat its source or was selected. Chemistry remained mixed. Similar typical size and ring counts conceal more peroxide and sulfur-triple-bond products alongside fewer nitrogen- and oxygen-halogen bonds; 80 of the 170 bypass admissions carry at least one defined concern marker. High labels do not establish stability or feasible geometry. Finally, all 135 affected Child batches stop with only six to nine observed retained-gate alternatives, so their unobserved replacements and alternative winners remain unknown.
finding_summary.results: Removal was exercised throughout the panel. All 435 batches contained the first ten valid fresh neighbors, with zero active tabu rejections, compared with 195 rejections in the Parent. The unchanged predicate identified 170 evaluated neighbors it would have vetoed on the actual Child history, spread over 135 batches and all 15 task sessions. Of these, 23 beat their source, 12 tied and 135 lost; nine strictly improved the archive and 29 became the next state. Across all proposals, source wins rose from 468 to 496 and strict archive updates from 238 to 269. Nevertheless, final macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.519484, a decrease of 0.002275 that narrowly meets the registered 0.002 prediction. Seed deltas were +0.021475, -0.037773 and +0.009471; their population deviation was 0.025574. Task mean changes were +0.006636 for zaleplon_mpo, -0.008325 for deco_hop, +0.039404 for drd2_docking, +0.007223 for median_2 and -0.056314 for sitagliptin_mpo. All runs completed with full validity. Raw generation attempts fell from 5303 to 5123, while recorded task runtime rose from 82.59 to 100.20 seconds.

molecular.headline: Aromatic ring families persist alongside peroxide bridges, reactive heteroatom halides and densely connected sulfur cages.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-045725e4628f was assessed against Parent n-abcd951ab7cc using the complete supplied seed panel: all fifteen trajectories per node, with 900 recorded molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task. The digest lists no tasks without trajectories. The bounded best and final excerpts are not balanced across seeds, so the seed descriptions below also use the full trajectories. Every cited SMILES is from the authoritative digest. The generated chemistry is ring-rich, with substantial aromatic content, carbonyls, amines, ethers, halogens and sulfur. Every task has ring-closure and branch token rates of 1.0; aromatic-token rates range from 0.8414 to 1.0. These are molecule-level string-presence rates, not fractions of atoms or chemically proven aromatic rings. Passive RDKit reading of the Child proposals gives 21–52 heavy atoms and 1–10 perceived basis rings, with medians of 33 and 4. The Parent has corresponding ranges of 21–53 and 2–10, with the same medians. Distinct seed walks reach different frameworks, but the best excerpts often contain closely related variants of one framework. Chemical plausibility is mixed and often poor near the observed maxima. Under identical graph-marker definitions, Child versus Parent proposals containing an O–O single bond number 360 versus 55; sulfur triple bonds 187 versus 95; N–halogen bonds 383 versus 500; O–halogen bonds 189 versus 301; and hydrogen-bearing sulfur with total valence above two 1234 versus 1247. These overlapping markers describe structures, not measured reactivity. The O–O motif persists in 33 Child selected states versus no Parent selected states. Among the 170 accepted Child molecules tagged by the saved logs as retained-predicate would-veto admissions, 80 carry at least one of the defined concern markers; their median size and ring count are 32.5 heavy atoms and 4 basis rings. This subset is not chemically clean and does not establish an individual motif contribution. All task digests have charge and stereocentre-token rates of 0.0. RDKit identifies unassigned tetrahedral centres in 3318 of the 4350 Child proposals, while no proposal has a stored atom chiral tag. Formal neutrality does not mean that an amine could not protonate. Four accepted Child molecules are logged direct aromatic nitrogen positional exchanges, compared with ten in the Parent; this narrow subset does not characterize whole-walk chemistry. The passive audit and definitions are recorded in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0013-02-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json. No candidate execution, new molecule generation, scoring, conformer calculation or synthetic route assessment was performed. The observations support missing chemical controls and comparisons, not a known absent target pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals contain 21–30 heavy atoms and 1–5 RDKit basis rings; the typical framework has three rings. Indole or benzothiophene cores carry an aryl carboxamide, with methoxy/ethoxy, methyl, amino, hydroxy or thiol substitutions. The seed-0 best is a 24-heavy-atom benzothiophene carboxamide with an aniline, methoxy group and chloromethyl substituent. The seed-1 best is a 23-heavy-atom indole carboxamide with ethoxy and aryl-thiol groups. The seed-2 best is a 26-heavy-atom benzothiophene hydrazide bearing N–Cl, chloromethyl, phenol and amino groups. These recognizable aromatic/carbonyl families coexist with late ring disruption and highly unusual sulfur bonding. The digest aromatic-token rate is 0.9655 and halogen-token rate 0.7575.
liabilities: The maximum contains an N–Cl hydrazide and a benzylic halide; the latter is a potential electrophilic site, while the N–Cl connection is a chemical-stability concern.

The digest also includes a ring-embedded C–S triple bond at hydrogen-bearing sulfur, hydroxylamine/hydrazine connections, disrupted aromatic rings and a strained small-ring aniline variant. Passing a molecular parser does not establish their synthetic feasibility.
missing_features: Stable, minimally substituted versions of the high-score aryl-carbonyl arrangement are not established for the N-chlorinated hydrazide maximum; the existing conventional amide examples show that ordinary linkages are accessible.
Late products do not consistently retain the compact aromatic geometry supported by the stronger observations. The data do not identify a particular absent target functional group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 benzothiophene amide reaches 0.40465559506276, while an early derivative that replaces the acyl linkage by a branched aminoalkyl connection scores 0.03343008011310944. Extending the seed-0 aromatic substituent into a longer oxygen/nitrogen-containing chain gives 0.05122719925570397. The visible gradient therefore favors a compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement over these disrupted or extended alternatives. The seed-2 chloromethyl and bromomethyl hydrazides tie at 0.41885833432199493, so those observations do not establish a preference between those halogens. Parent best scores for seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.393567030299894, 0.39905049777278273 and 0.41003927643747895. The Child retains the identical seed-1 best; the other seed maxima remain within the same fused-ring/carbonyl chemistry, with changed heteroatom placement and linkages. Several later sulfur-triple-bond products still score around 0.398, so the label does not reliably reject chemically troubling bond environments.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals are relatively large: 30–52 heavy atoms, with a median of 39 and 2–7 perceived basis rings. Aromatic-token presence is 1.0. The seed-2 maximum has 50 heavy atoms and three perceived aromatic rings: a pyrimidinedione-like core with exocyclic unsaturation, an anilino decoration and a substituted pyridyl side chain. Long alkyl and aminoether appendages carry both O–F and O–Cl bonds. Close high-scoring variants retain the original fused pyrrole/dione arrangement. Full trajectories show different seed outcomes: seed 0 reaches a decorated aryl/pyrrole system with thiocarbonyl and N–Cl groups, whereas seed 1 reaches a heteroaromatic assembly with a consecutive oxygen chain containing multiple O–O bonds. The 247 O–O-containing Child proposals contrast with ten in the Parent for this task.
liabilities: The seed-2 maximum contains a hypofluorite-like aryl O–F connection and an alkyl O–Cl connection; these are not ordinary carbon-bound fluorine or chlorine substituents.

The other seed walks include polyperoxide, N–Cl and unusual unsaturated sulfur or ring-bond environments. Long flexible branches and unassigned stereogenic sites add uncertainty about accessible conformations and practical synthesis.
missing_features: Ordinary, stable attachments that preserve the high-score aromatic and polar-group arrangement without O–halogen or peroxide bonds are not established for the leading Child family.
Smaller matched decorations retaining the useful core environments are insufficient to identify a minimal chemical requirement. The observed ties leave some appendage chemistry unresolved.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. Low optimizer examples at 0.5286081645773063 and 0.5307397206374189 disrupt a carbonyl or an aromatic decoration. The seed-2 maximum reaches 0.6151877133105802; its closely related fused-core counterpart scores 0.6132655914980889. Thus useful decorated aromatic/heteroatom environments persist across different central ring connections, with extensive growth tolerated. Several side-chain variants tie at 0.613068261458674, and the compact initial bromide already has a baseline score of 0.5: these observations do not demonstrate that every added group contributes. Child seed maxima are 0.5993058722196889, 0.5910590773526239 and 0.6151877133105802; the Parent counterparts are 0.6161710037174721, 0.605139548855754 and 0.6092182584436399. Both panels retain heavily decorated aromatic families with questionable peripheral bonds; the changed labels do not map to a uniform chemical-quality change.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals have 29–43 heavy atoms and 3–9 perceived basis rings, with a median of five rings. Aromatic-token presence is 1.0 and halogen-token presence 0.9989. The best excerpt is concentrated entirely in seed 0: its maximum is a 31-heavy-atom scaffold combining an N-methyl tetrahydroisoquinoline-like ring, a substituted azetidine connected through a methylene, a thioether, a methoxy arene and chlorinated carbon substituents. It contains five basis rings, including a three/five-member fused carbon system whose aromatic atom notation should not be mistaken for an ordinary benzene. Seed 1 instead reaches a bridged polyaromatic amine framework; seed 2 reaches a nitrogen-rich cage containing unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur and an O–S attachment. These are distinct chemical outcomes hidden by a pooled best excerpt.
liabilities: The maximum combines an azetidine, a highly constrained three/five-member fused carbon fragment, a benzylic/alkyl chloride and unassigned stereogenic carbon sites. The saturated amine functionality itself is ordinary; its complete framework remains questionable.

Other high observations retain sulfur with both an attached hydrogen and unusually high valence, O–S links and densely connected nitrogen cages. The near-unit saved score supplies no independent synthetic or binding validation.
missing_features: The leading amine/hydrophobic arrangement lacks demonstrated analogues with ordinary, less strained ring topology and controlled relative stereochemistry.

The record does not establish the protonation or conformer populations associated with the high label. Basic cyclic amines are present, so a general lack of amine centres would be an incorrect diagnosis.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Low examples at 0.006989578671349273 and 0.007468397818197266 retain a carboxylic acid, amide and sulfonamide-substituted nitrogen with a large aromatic framework. The seed-0 maximum at 0.9999993080945268 has removed these carbonyl/acid features and presents ordinary tertiary cyclic amines beside hydrophobic ring surfaces. The association supports amine accessibility and its spatial relationship to the hydrophobic framework, rather than aromatic or halogen content alone, which is already present in weak products. It does not identify a docking pose, protonation state or experimental affinity. Parent seed maxima are 0.8856242185485628, 0.868020189804352 and 0.9148143511682032; Child values are 0.9999993080945268, 0.8407510650781277 and 0.9459193614427688. The Child seed-0 best replaces the Parent sulfur-rich unsaturated family with a simpler thioether/amine arrangement, but adds a strained fused carbon unit; the other seeds retain different cage or bridged-ring chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The 29–43-heavy-atom proposals contain 3–8 basis rings and almost always retain a carbonyl; 802 of 870 have an amide substructure. Aromatic-token presence is 1.0, while halogen-token presence is only 0.1931. The seed-0 maximum is a 32-heavy-atom structure with two phenyl rings, N-methyl groups, a seven-member lactam and a ten-member ring incorporating an N–O–O–aryl bridge. Seed 1 reaches a larger linked aryl/amine/lactam macrocycle, with a fourteen-member perceived ring. Seed 2 reaches a 35-heavy-atom, six-ring carbonyl/ether/amine assembly with fused and bridged connectivity. These remain descendants of the initial decorated heterocyclic dione rather than evidence of broad, independently sampled medicinal scaffold families.
liabilities: The highest observed family embeds an O–O bond adjacent to an N–O bond in a large ring, raising stability and synthesis concerns despite its recognizable lactam and aryl fragments.

Other products carry N–O/N–N sequences, large constrained macrocycles, unusual sulfur substitutions and ambiguous stereochemical relationships. Dense ring count alone is not evidence of a realizable conformation.
missing_features: Conventional ring closures that retain the stronger aryl/lactam arrangement without an N–O–O bridge remain unestablished for the leading family.
The supplied labels do not resolve which ring, linker and carbonyl geometry is essential. Stable, simpler matched frameworks and explicitly defined feasible configurations are missing comparisons.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329. Ring-opened carbonyl/urea or hydrazide-chain derivatives score 0.1263981386214515 and 0.12467972074136988, while the constrained seed-0 peroxide/lactam structure reaches 0.2156502008055363. Its shorter lactam-ring counterpart scores 0.2133448492432336, and the different seed-2 carbonyl/ether polycycle scores 0.20543286751574985. The visible gradient favors some constrained aryl/carbonyl arrangements over the displayed open-chain derivatives, without demonstrating that the peroxide bridge is a beneficial chemical feature. Parent seed maxima are 0.21196904390980506, 0.19092251395438758 and 0.20185639717998205; the Child counterparts are 0.2156502008055363, 0.20533438703265813 and 0.20543286751574985. Both panels reach constrained aromatic/carbonyl families. The Child replaces some Parent O–halogen and unusual sulfur exposure with peroxide-rich ring chemistry, which is a trade in liabilities rather than a proven quality improvement.

per_task.generated_character: These are the most sulfur-dominated constrained products: 26–36 heavy atoms, 3–10 perceived basis rings, and a median of six rings. Every proposal contains a carbonyl, and 713 of 870 contain a perceived three- or four-member ring. Aromatic-token presence is 0.8414, yet a high seed-2 example has no RDKit-perceived aromatic ring. The seed-0 maximum contains 34 heavy atoms, seven basis rings, fluorinated carbon substituents, carbonyl heterocycles, five sulfur atoms, an N–Cl connection, a sulfur–sulfur triple bond and further unusual sulfur multiple bonds. Seed 1 reaches an acyl-fluoride-containing sulfur cage; seed 2 reaches a mostly nonaromatic polycycle with small unsaturated sulfur rings. The recognizable N/O/carbonyl components do not make the surrounding sulfur networks ordinary medicinal chemistry.
liabilities: Hydrogen-bearing sulfur at high valence, S–S or C–S triple bonds, non-oxo sulfur multiple bonds, N–Cl or S–F connections and acyl fluorides occur among strong observations. Several are qualitatively severe chemical-plausibility concerns.

Many short rings, shared bridge atoms and unspecified stereochemical relationships concentrate geometric strain. Aromatic tokens, a sanitized graph and a saved score are insufficient evidence that these complete structures could be isolated or synthesized.
missing_features: Ordinary fluorinated carbon/nitrogen/oxygen frameworks reproducing the locally favored size and polar-group balance without exotic sulfur networks are not established by the observed high-score families.

Geometrically feasible, stereochemically specified alternatives are missing for the constrained sulfur-rich products. The supplied scores do not identify a particular missing target amine or heterocycle.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: A relatively conventional initial-family ring-expanded dione derivative scores 7.590554525032884e-10, but a densely sulfur-substituted cage also scores only 2.5751054098011344e-09. Thus more sulfur or more rings alone does not explain the gradient. The seed-0 maximum reaches 0.47628381509500306. Closely related single- versus triple-bond sulfur variants both score 0.45634604420642844, showing that this chemically consequential bond change is unresolved by those labels. In seed 2, extending a fluorinated exocyclic substituent in the otherwise matching sulfur framework changes the observed score from 0.4386188333472739 to 0.11738262097323607. Local size and substitution balance matter within the peculiar framework, but the trajectories do not reveal a conventional target pharmacophore. Parent seed maxima are 0.48118636011729826, 0.5903526424693334 and 0.4484554129767839; Child counterparts are 0.47628381509500306, 0.4284269334996555 and 0.44634282685969023. Both panels retain dense sulfur cages despite their different recorded maxima.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Actual high-score examples retain N–halogen, O–halogen, peroxide and unusual sulfur bonds. Across the complete Child proposals, 360 contain an O–O single bond and 187 contain a sulfur triple bond; 33 actual selected states retain O–O. Close single- versus triple-bond sulfur variants have the identical saved score 0.45634604420642844, so observed score preference is insufficient to distinguish their chemical plausibility.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain ordinary heteroatom bond environments as it modifies otherwise recognizable molecular frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic chemical generator needs access to ordinary, stable heteroatom linkages as matched alternatives around its own successful frameworks. Evaluate those alternatives through normal feedback; these observations do not justify assuming that reactive bonds are useful or that blanket removal improves scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The proposals span 1–10 RDKit basis rings, and 1340 of 4350 contain a three- or four-member basis ring. Observed best products include a constrained three/five-member fused carbon unit, peroxide-bearing macrocycles and multiply bridged sulfur cages. The ring-rich outputs therefore lack evidence of practical three-dimensional realizability, not ring content.
transferable_gaps.gap: Feasible ring geometry is not established by the generator’s extensive ring construction and atom-level validity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically ordinary ring-size and linkage alternatives that preserve the useful attachment arrangement while varying unnecessary constraints. Geometric feasibility must be addressed explicitly before treating a ring-rich graph as a makeable scaffold; this is a generator property independent of the objective label.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Several leading decorations contain long alkyl/aminoether branches and heteroatom halides. Multiple side-chain variants tie at 0.613068261458674, and chloromethyl/bromomethyl variants tie at 0.41885833432199493. Conversely, loss of an acyl connection or expansion of particular linkers can sharply lower the recorded label. Neither arbitrary growth nor indiscriminate simplification is supported.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not establish a minimal, stable set of decorations around its higher-scoring frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose matched simplifications and linkage changes that preserve the principal ring and polar-group arrangement. Use the observed response to distinguish useful attachments from avoidable complexity, without targeting a named objective or presuming that compactness always helps.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. Passive RDKit perception finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 3318 of 4350 Child proposals, and none has a stored atom chiral tag. Displayed strong molecules include substituted saturated amine rings and densely bridged heteroatom frameworks; the complete stereochemical molecules are therefore not specified.
transferable_gaps.gap: Defined stereochemical identity is absent even when the generated connectivity creates potential stereogenic centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve feasible configurations where the graph supports stereogenic centres, with chemically coherent alternatives for constrained frameworks. This fills an identity and chemistry gap; the supplied observations do not demonstrate that configuration changes improve the score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Within individual seeds the best excerpts cluster around one aromatic/carbonyl, cyclic-amine or sulfur-cage family. The full Child panel contains only four accepted direct aromatic nitrogen positional exchanges. Basic cyclic amines are present, but equivalent ordinary placements of carbonyls, heteroaromatic nitrogens and linkers are not systematically established by the output.
transferable_gaps.gap: The observed polar-group arrangements remain concentrated in heavily modified descendants of a few inherited frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broaden coherent matched changes in heteroatom placement and polar-linker connection while retaining otherwise useful topology. Let the generator’s own feedback determine which arrangements matter; a single missing target-specific group cannot be inferred from these trajectories.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
